title: gpu-oom-investigation-hypotheses
content:
Context:
- Short session notes while chasing a flakey GPU OOM on a dev box (rtx-a5000-ish). Intermittent: sometimes training a small transformer hits OOM right away, other times it completes. Suspect a driver/runtime mismatch + memory fragmentation + container shim issues.

Observed symptoms (quick list):
- Python runtime reports RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.20 GiB (GPU 0; total capacity 23.69 GiB; reserved 2.34 GiB)
- At other times, container fails to even import torch with: "error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- dmesg occasionally shows GPU pages evicted / TTM warnings (sparse, not constant).

Commands tried and snippets (timestamps local):
- nvidia-smi (2024-11-03 09:12):
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
  | NVIDIA-SMI 535.113.01    Driver Version: 535.113.01    CUDA Version: 12.1     |
  | GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
  |  0   A5000             On        00000000:3B:00.0 Off |                  0 |
  +-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

- python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available())" ->
  2.2.0 11.7 True
  Note: torch built with CUDA 11.7 but system driver reports CUDA 12.1. This mismatch is suspicious.

- Container runtime: docker run --gpus all --rm -it redwood-dev:latest /bin/bash\  -> inside container: ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so | grep libcuda
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f8d...)
  ldconfig -p | grep libcuda -> points to /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (driver provided by host)

- grep in dmesg for NVRM / GPU (2024-11-03 09:20):
  [  5128.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID=8472, GPU has fallen off the bus.
  [  5128.123789] NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
  These correlate with the times we saw python segfault or fail to allocate memory.

- strace when importing torch (2024-11-03 09:25):
  execve("/usr/bin/python3", ["python3", "-c", ...], ...) = 0
  openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = 3
  read(3, "\177ELF...") = 832
  mmap(NULL, 8192, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, 3, 0) = 0x7f8d7f000000
  ...
  write(2, "Fatal Python error: Segmentation fault\n", 30) = 30

- Minimal repro (repro_oom.py) used to iterate:
  import torch
  a = [torch.empty((1024,1024,512), dtype=torch.float16, device='cuda') for _ in range(50)]
  -> reproducible OOM sometimes; other runs pass (racey).

Hypotheses / quick analysis:
1) Driver vs runtime compatibility: torch was built with CUDA 11.7 but driver reports CUDA 12.1. Usually driver >= runtime is OK, but the segfaults and libcuda library path differences make me wonder about multiple driver installs (host vs kernel modules mismatch).
2) Container host-bind mismatch: host libcuda present, but kernel module might be older; if nvidia-container-toolkit mounts a different libcuda, it could be ABI incompatible.
3) Fragmentation + pinned allocations: earlier reserved memory (2.34 GiB) suggests other processes or leftover allocations (system daemons, previous containers not cleaned). Mixed allocator settings (older torch with caching allocator) cause fragmentation and failure to reuse.
4) Faulty GPU HW or PCIe link flakiness: "GPU has fallen off the bus" dmesg entries point to possible hardware/firmware. Might be thermal/BIOS or bad riser on this test node.
5) Driver bug in 535.x for this card + kernel version (we saw some reports on distro forums).

What I've tried to mitigate so far:
- Rebooted host to ensure driver kernel module reload. After reboot, nvidia-smi reports same driver but some of the kernel XIDs dropped.
- Ran container with --gpus all and --cap-add SYS_PTRACE to capture more logs.
- Set PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128 to lower fragmentation (re-run: slight improvement, but not resolved).
- Explicit torch.cuda.empty_cache() between runs; added torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(). Reduced frequency of OOM but not eliminated.
- Pulled a cudatoolkit-aligned image (pytorch image built with CUDA 12.1) and ran there; import succeeded but runtime training still had sporadic OOM + occasional "GPU fell off the bus". That points more at host/driver/hardware.

Additional command outputs collected for triage:
- uname -a: Linux dev-node-07 6.1.0-23-generic #25-Ubuntu SMP x86_64 GNU/Linux
- dkms status: nvidia, 535.113.01, 6.1.0-23-generic, x86_64: installed
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version -> NVRM version: 535.113.01
- lspci -vvv -s 3b:00.0 shows: Link Sta: Speed 8GT/s, Width x16 (ok) but occasional Correctable errors: 10

Short-term playbook / next steps:
- Reproduce under nvtop / watch nvidia-smi -l 1 to capture the moment of OOM and cross reference with dmesg.
- Swap this node with a known-good node to see if symptom follows container (if it does, it's likely software).
- Boot with driver 535 -> try rolling back to 525 or to the distro-provided driver to see if segfaults and XIDs stop.
- Run nvidia-device-plugin tests and run a stress test (cuda-memtest or simple CUDA allocator loops) to check for HW faults.
- Add structured nightly job to run the small repro multiple times to get deterministic fail rate and capture core dumps (enable coredump for python).

Notes / random breadcrumbs:
- Found a Slack thread where one person saw "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" when host had 12.1 driver and container had libs for 11.7 — they fixed by using host driver + container matching libs.
- Checked for multiple libcuda versions under /usr/lib and /usr/local; there were stale leftovers in /usr/local/lib which were being picked up in some runs. Removing them helped import stability.
- When import fails with libcuda not found, it was due to a chroot overlay (we had an old build script that copied a subset of host libs into /opt/app/libs). Cleaned that overlay.

Debug checklist to run when this happens again (short):
- nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/nvsmilog.txt
- sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-gpu.txt
- python -c "import torch,sys; print(torch.__version__, torch.version.cuda, torch.cuda.is_available()); print(torch.cuda.mem_get_info())" 2>&1 | tee /tmp/torch-info.txt
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch,os; print(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(torch.__file__), "lib/libtorch_cuda.so"))') | grep libcuda > /tmp/ldd-libcuda.txt || true
- ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda* /usr/local/lib/libcuda* || true

If I had to guess (based on current data): mixed blame between driver install artifacts + memory fragmentation. Priority: confirm hardware health (stress test) then isolate driver (swap/rollback), then force container images whose CUDA runtime exactly matches torch build.

Open questions for Diego / Priya:
- Have we seen this pattern in CI nodes after the kernel update last month? (could be correlated)
- Any automated health dashboards that alert on XID counts per node? We should add that if not.

To capture: will run one long-run reproducer under nvprof / Nsight Systems and attach trace to PR referenced above.

End of scratchpad.
